newsitem.title: FRANCE: National Front officially takes over French town.
newsitem.headline: National Front officially takes over French town.

text.p: Leftists demonstrated on Sunday when France's extreme right-wing National Front party officially took control of the town hall in this southern town where it won a sweeping muncipal election victory last week.
Catherine Megret, wife of NF number two Bruno Megret was elected Vitrolles mayor at the first meeting of the new Front-dominated municipal council.

Outgoing Socialist mayor Jean-Jacques Anglade led left-wing councillors in a symbolic walk-out from the session, whistling "Le Chant des Partisans," hymn of France's World War Two Resistance movement.
Several hundred leftist militants massed outside the building chanting protests against the FN but strong police forces specially drafted into the town prevented violence.
Catherine Megret called for "Vitrolles to return to calm and serenity".
Vitrolles is the fourth town in southern France town taken over by the FN. The others are Toulon, Marignane and Orange.
The Vitrolles victory coincided with snowballing protests by intellectuals against a tough new cabinet-sanctioned draft immigration bill.

Intellectuals say the bill mirrors the ideas of FN leader Jean-Marie Le Pen and is meant to show voters that the centre-right government can do just as well as the anti-immigration FN in cracking down on foreigners.

The protests have included publication of separate lists of hundreds of scientists, artists, doctors and actors calling on the public to flout the new law if it is voted by parliament later this month.
Signatories among more than 400 actors and actresses included Jeanne Moreau and Catherine Deneuve.
The new bill will require people supplying certificates to foreigners saying they will take responsibility for them during their stay in France to also declare when their guests leave.

Would-be visitors from many Third World countries who cannot show they have enough money to fund a long visit to France are currently granted visas only if they can provide a certificate showing someone in France will provide them with lodging.

The new article, like the certificates before them, are aimed at discouraging would-be illegal immigrants of which there are an estimated one million in France. There are a further four million foreigners legally resident in the country.

But requiring individuals to report to police that their guests had left has raised a storm of protest among the intellectuals who are likening the requirement to laws of the wartime Vichy collaborationkst regime.
Prime Minister Alain Juppe has said the government will stand by the draft and the mainstream Socialist-Communist opposition has been conspicuously absent from the protests against it.
